criteria.statement: A G4 approval cannot authorize a later source commit; a fresh synthetic fixture approval restores only that fixture's transition.
A preplanted temporary hardlink cannot redirect atomic publication onto an outside sentinel.
Fast-lane validation can execute a recorded child Aegis operation without holding its parent state lease.
The actual lane cap changes, malformed limits/paths refuse, and unknown app scopes do not mutate the root pipeline.
The 2026-10-17 post-release audit regressions (hook identity, link traversal, slice identity, lock and uninstall edges) are committed failing-first tests and pass on the repaired source.

review_provenance: Scoped fresh-context model reviews plus conductor reconciliation and runnable regressions, including the 2026-10-17 post-release adversarial pass on the shipped v0.10.0. Not an independent human security certification or G4 approval.

findings.summary: State, memory, path-ownership and recovery findings were repaired, re-reviewed and independently reverified by the conductor; the ledger links their negative controls.
Ref aliases, nested recovery identities, malformed receipts, mutable source checks and competing-result false passes have explicit regression coverage and repairs.
Fresh builds, built-asset packaging, caller-owned source approval and accurate scope/limitations replace the prior misleading release paths. Final CI, artifact and human gates are still required.

Shipped v0.10.0 clobbered or deleted foreign hooks that merely mentioned the marker, wrote through symlinked hook files, and installed hooks through a linked .git. Banner-anchored identity, explicit link refusals and re-init refusal with a named backup now cover these paths.

Slice removal closed lanes for moved worktrees, lock edges raw-crashed or misdiagnosed corruption, and uninstall could half-complete around a pinned .aegis or an external hooksPath. Branch-identity registry checks, fail-closed lock recovery guidance, machine-tree-first uninstall and skip-with-note external hooks are verified by regressions.

Legacy strict flags, structural doc heuristics, unavailable host capabilities, power-loss durability and comparative/small-executor effectiveness retain the limits stated in the release contract and queued v0.11 plan. The immutable v0.10.0 tag retains the pre-repair defects; the post-release repairs fold into the next release and no published tag moves.
